newsitem.title: USA: Tambrands to close four plants, expand others.
newsitem.headline: Tambrands to close four plants, expand others.

text.p: Tambrands Inc. said Wednesday it will phase out four manufacturing facilities and upgrade and consolidate production in its remaining five factories to combine its separate Americas and International groups into a single, more efficient global organisation.
The White Plains, N.Y.-based maker of Tampax tampons and other feminine hygiene products said it plans to close plants in Rutland, Vt., Tours, France, Tipperary, Ireland and St. Petersburg, Russia.
Manufacturing facilities in Auburn, Me. and Havant, England will be expanded to become hub locations.
The new global structure and plant consolidation will result in a net reduction of about 600 jobs, or 17 percent of Tambrands' worldwide work force, the company said.
Investors showed their approval by boosting Tambrands stock $2.375 to $44.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The restructuring will include the elimination of approximately 1,100 jobs and the addition of 500 new jobs in the upgraded manufacturing facilities and in marketing and new product development.
As a result of the moves, Tambrands will take a charge of $46 million before tax, or $1.00 a share after tax, in the third quarter of 1996.

Edward Fogarty, who joined Tambrands as president and chief executive officer in 1994, will assume the additional position of chairman of the board, succeeding Howard Wentz, the company said. Wentz will remain a director.
The company said it expects the reorganization to result in recurring annual savings of about $20 million before tax and to be fully phased in by the beginning of 1998.
"In order to accelerate our growth, we must become an even more effective global competitor," said Fogarty.

"If we are to keep winning against much larger companies, we need to be leaner, faster and more efficient in building the Tampax brand with new products, product improvements, education and advertising," he said.
